issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a SealSaloon method calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but both the template's example usage (Main.java) and the solution implement and call a method named computeMealCost(Meal). This name mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about which method to implement and which name to use in their implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to computeMealCost(Meal): int, or (B) rename computeMealCost in the template and solution to calculateTotalPrice with the same signature and update usages in Main accordingly. Ensure the chosen name is used consistently in the UML, problem text, template examples, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute the net cost of a Meal, but the solution repository introduces a differently named method computeMealCost(Meal). The template's commented Main also refers to computeMealCost, while the solution's Main calls calculateTotalPrice — producing inconsistent identifiers across artifacts for the same conceptual operation (computing a meal's total price). This mismatch creates confusion for students about which method name to implement or call and may cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Prefer the name from the problem statement (calculateTotalPrice) to match the UML: rename computeMealCost(Meal) in SealSaloon to public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and update all callers (Main and any template comments) accordingly. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use computeMealCost if that name is preferred — but ensure all code and docs use the same identifier.
